title: None of the 12 rehearsals (alarm, reboot, backup restore, key rotation, bad deploy, delete request) has ever been run
evidence: docs/readiness/DRILLS.md 'Summary log' rows 1 to 12 all say 'never' with empty 'Last run', 'Result' and 'Open fix'; the file has one commit (696ef20, 2026-11-18) and no later commit mentions a drill (git log checked 2026-11-21). Outside lists: Google SRE launch checklist 'Data backup/restore, disaster recovery' and 'How to terminate or restart without affecting clients or users' (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/); AWS Well-Architected reliability 'Test reliability' and 'Plan for Disaster Recovery (DR)' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/reliability.html). A drill may have been run on the Mac without being written down; the file cannot show that.
fix: Run drills 1, 3 and 5 first (alarm, restore onto a second machine, rotate one key), write the result in the summary log the same day; the rest after launch.
fix_cost: about 3 hours for the three; no money
dup_of: R58 and R02 cover restore and alarm as risks; new: the whole rehearsal list is unrun, so every recovery step in RUNBOOK.md is untested text

title: No business insurance of any kind has been priced, and the plan to stay a sole proprietor never weighed it
evidence: grep 'insurance' over launch-gaps, REGISTER, FINDINGS, RUNBOOK, HANDOVER and legal-review-2026-11-17.md: no line about business, cyber or liability cover. legal-review-2026-11-17.md Q19: incorporation 'also protects personal assets, which matters little at Pexi's current risk'. Outside: Insurance Bureau of Canada, 'Cyber insurance can cover "The loss of, unauthorized access to and/or disclosure of confidential or personal information."' and 'Your professional liability isn't covered under a home insurance policy.' (https://ibc.ca/insurance-basics/business/types-of-business-insurance-coverage). IBC does not say business insurance is required. A broker-site search snippet put a basic general liability policy near CA$450 a year; that figure is unchecked. Pexi holds shopper data on an unencrypted home laptop (FileVault off), so a theft is the case cyber cover is written for.
fix: One broker quote request for cyber plus general liability for a sole proprietor working from home, and a call to the home-insurance provider asking whether a business server in the house is covered. Then decide to buy or accept the risk in writing.
fix_cost: 1 hour; premium unknown until quoted (assumed a few hundred dollars a year)
dup_of: round3 blind 'Personal liability and employer claims' says 'no insurance' in passing; new: IBC wording, the home-policy exclusion, and that the sole-proprietor ruling never considered insurance as the substitute for incorporating

title: Every deploy hard-kills the server, with no drain, so in-flight scans fail on each push
evidence: mac/deploy/deployer.mjs line 234: launchctl kickstart -k <server>; grep for SIGTERM, SIGINT, server.close and drain in app/server.ts and app/src found no shutdown handler (only unhandledRejection at app/server.ts:2456). The checker deploys every passing push to main within about 30 s. Restart window is tracked (deployer.mjs line 66, 6 minutes) but that only silences alarms. Outside: SRE launch checklist 'How to terminate or restart without affecting clients or users' (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/). Not measured: how many requests a restart drops. SQLite files survive a kill (write-ahead log), so this is dropped requests, not corruption (assumed).
fix: On SIGTERM stop accepting, wait up to 5 s for open requests, then exit; use plain kickstart (no -k) or send SIGTERM first. Also pushes during busy hours are the exposure: add a quiet-hours note to RELEASE-CHECKLIST.
dup_of: R09 covers a bad deploy; new: the normal good deploy also drops live requests

title: Dependency checks were done once (2026-11-16) and there is no routine; the phone build tool still has 1 high and 6 moderate advisories today
evidence: Ran npm audit --omit=dev on 2026-11-21: app 0, spine 0, native 7 vulnerabilities (6 moderate, 1 high: brace-expansion, glob, minimatch, uuid, xcode, @capacitor/cli), same as docs/security-check/v1-v2-v6-secrets-static-phone.md L6 written five days earlier, 'fix available via npm audit fix'. No dependabot or renovate file, no scheduled audit in .github/workflows (only server-alarm.yml) or mac/launchd. docs/readiness/raw/external-coverage.md line 77 marked 'Dependency vulnerability updates' n/a. L6 says the native advisories are in the build tool and not in the shipped app, so impact today is low. Outside: AWS Well-Architected 'Learn and evolve from events' and 'Implement change' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/operational-excellence.html); OWASP API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration (https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10).
fix: Run npm audit fix in native/ at the next build; add a monthly calendar line or a scheduled job that runs npm audit in app, spine, catalogue and native and emails only on a new high.
fix_cost: 30 minutes once, 5 minutes a month; no money
dup_of: FINDINGS L6 and R85/R86; new: no routine, and the numbers are unchanged since 11-16

title: Delete-my-data is a manual 30-day job for one person on one Mac, and the 10,000-user volume was never worked out
evidence: docs/privacy/data-requests.md: requests arrive by email, 30-day clock, 'On the Mac, in the repo folder, run the script. Export first, then delete'; Delete my data in the app only opens an email (you.js:119-129 per that doc); only /api/scan-rating/delete exists as a server delete route (app/server.ts:4154). Drill 4 for it has never run (DRILLS.md). Volume assumption (not measured, no source): if 0.5 to 1 percent of 10,000 phones ask in a year that is 50 to 100 requests, each needing identity check, script, RevenueCat click and a reply. During the May 2027 internship or a Mac outage the 30-day clock still runs.
fix: Add a server route that deletes by device id when the request carries that phone's own key, so the common case needs no human; keep the email path for the rest. Or accept manual handling and write the expected monthly count into the launch plan.
fix_cost: half a day for the route; zero to accept
dup_of: R51 and R63 (found); new: scale view, and that the in-app button is not a delete

title: Correction to round 3 blind: the app does send error reports, and the injection surfaces I checked hold
evidence: app/server.ts:4296 route /api/client-error and app/public/js/crash-report.js exist (blind said error telemetry unknown). XSS: app/public/js/lib/dom.js escapeHtml and the html tagged template escape every interpolation; shop names go through escapeHtml in camera.js:2223; CSP meta is injected into the native bundle by native/scripts/sync-web.mjs:189. Claude price ask: identify/src/range-ask.ts validateRange rejects extra fields, non-integer or non-positive cents, a currency mismatch, a unit over 80 chars and any high above a ceiling, so a hostile product name cannot return a freeform answer beyond a short unit string. OWASP API7 SSRF: the only outside fetch inputs found were barcodes and map squares (src/open-food-facts.ts:158); barcode validation before the URL was not read. Live probe: 12 guessed paths (/health /metrics /debug /admin /openapi.json /.env /.git/config /package.json /server.ts /api/v1/ /api/v2/ /api/admin) all 404, and a cross-origin OPTIONS preflight got 403 (OWASP API9 improper inventory, API8 misconfiguration). About 24 live requests used, all GET or OPTIONS, no consent header.
dup_of: round3 blind 'No crash or error telemetry in the app'; FINDINGS covers the rest
